reuse.why: Collapses the inline midpoint copies into shared helpers and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but the API field uses the older getScheduledAmount, which ignores the operator, instead of the new getPlannedAmount used everywhere else.

duplication.why: getPlannedAmount and getScheduledAmount now both carry their own null/number/range dispatch over the shared getRangeAmount, a parallel pair of amount helpers in the same file.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and server call sites (forecast, schedule actions, posting, preview, budget template) delegate to it.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field; the multi-line comment edits are slightly messy but nothing unrelated is touched.

maintainability.why: A maintainer must know that getPlannedAmount is the full rule while getScheduledAmount (API and UI) silently skips the approximate case, so the two can disagree for 'isapprox' schedules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts expectedAmount uses getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount) without the operator instead of getPlannedAmount; desktop-client consumers of getScheduledAmount also skip the approximate rule

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts: getScheduledAmount and getPlannedAmount restate the same null/number/range dispatch under two names, differing only by inversion and the isapprox branch

abstraction_drift.where: getPlannedAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch across the steps; api-models.ts expectedAmount bypasses it via getScheduledAmount, which has no op
